step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows a multi-tenant event processing and customer engagement system from Capillary Technologies. First, configurers define events through ALB into a Kubernetes cluster (K8S) which writes event definitions and metadata into DynamoDB. Third-party systems send events to API Gateway, triggering a Webhook Lambda function that validates and verifies the tenant/event using metadata stored in DynamoDB before pushing the event payload to SQS. SQS triggers a Processor Lambda function, which persists raw/analyzed events into DynamoDB and streams actionable events into Kinesis. Finally, Workers consume events from Kinesis to trigger business actions (points allocation, promotions, messaging).

graph.name: Capillary Multi-Tenant Event Processing Architecture
graph.notes: Handles up to 10 million events a day with heavy burst volume support via serverless components.

nodes.notes: Platform users defining custom tenant events and attributes.

nodes.notes: Application Load Balancer entry point for API access.

nodes.name: K8S
nodes.notes: Kubernetes cluster running event definition APIs.

nodes.name: DYNAMODB
nodes.notes: Stores event metadata definitions and persistent processed event data.

nodes.name: Third-Party System
nodes.notes: External client systems registering webhooks and sending runtime events.

nodes.name: API GW
nodes.notes: Entry point for webhook event ingest.

nodes.name: WEBHOOK
nodes.notes: Validates tenant/event metadata against DynamoDB and pushes to queue. Scales rapidly during traffic bursts.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Buffers incoming webhook events for downstream processing.

nodes.name: PROCESSOR
nodes.notes: Consumes SQS messages, persists data, and pushes stream events to Kinesis.

nodes.name: KINESIS
nodes.notes: Streams processed events for async worker actions.

nodes.name: WORKERS
nodes.notes: Workers running inside platform that perform actions like point allocation and notifications.

edges.notes: ALB forwards configuration calls to K8S cluster.
K8S saves event definition metadata to DynamoDB.
Third-party systems send runtime webhook events.
Webhook Lambda reads event metadata and authentication details from DynamoDB.
Webhook Lambda pushes verified events into SQS.
Processor Lambda persists raw event data into DynamoDB for analytics.
Processor Lambda streams actionable events to Kinesis.
Workers consume events from Kinesis to trigger backend business logic.
